statementMapping.constructedDataBasis: Fictional patient measurements, chronology, pathology and acquisition records; not empirical rates, universal treatment cutoffs or medication doses. Laboratory intervals are those of the constructed record.
statementMapping.extensionLimitations: Unchanged atoms retain original dates. Explicit offline extensions and option rankings carry targeted verification holds; no source retrieval or clinical sign-off.

claims.statement: After diagnostic imaging identifies an accessible suspicious solid breast mass, image-guided core biopsy can establish a tissue diagnosis before definitive excision planning.
claims.limitation: This pathway excludes clinically urgent infection and does not prescribe a particular imaging modality or biopsy device. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an accessible solid breast mass categorized as suspicious on completed diagnostic imaging.

claims.statement: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.
claims.limitation: The vessel relationship classifies anatomy but does not establish acuity or select a repair technique. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose operative or imaging report directly describes a groin hernia's relationship to the inferior epigastric vessels.

claims.statement: Fine pleomorphic or fine linear or fine linear-branching calcifications are suspicious morphologies, and a linear or segmental distribution can add concern when interpreted with morphology and the complete examination.
claims.limitation: No morphology or distribution descriptor independently establishes cancer. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose mammographic assessment includes breast calcifications.

claims.statement: Vascular, large rod-like, rim, layering, and coarse densely calcified patterns are among calcification appearances categorized as typically benign in the current mammography lexicon.
claims.limitation: The classification belongs within the complete radiologist assessment and cannot override other suspicious findings. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose mammographic assessment includes breast calcifications.

claims.statement: Mammographic mass density is one descriptor and must be interpreted with shape, margin, associated features, comparison imaging, and the final radiologist assessment rather than being used alone to diagnose or exclude malignancy.
claims.limitation: The approved questions do not assign a final BI-RADS category from density alone. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose diagnostic mammogram includes a described breast mass.

claims.statement: An irregular mammographic mass with a spiculated margin is a concerning morphologic combination that warrants suspicious assessment rather than benign reassurance.
claims.limitation: Imaging morphology raises or lowers concern but is not itself a tissue diagnosis. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing diagnostic mammographic assessment of a breast mass.

claims.statement: Suspicious breast imaging warrants the indicated diagnostic pathway and does not by itself establish a cancer diagnosis or authorize cancer-directed surgery without tissue diagnosis.
claims.limitation: This package teaches imaging-feature recognition only; biopsy technique and cancer treatment are separate concepts. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with breast imaging assessed as suspicious or highly suggestive of malignancy.

claims.statement: For a woman age 30 to 39 with a new palpable breast mass, diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis and targeted breast ultrasound are appropriate components of the initial diagnostic imaging evaluation.
claims.limitation: Only one adequate authoritative source is mapped. The exact combined-order question wording and distractors remain pending named-clinician review. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Nonpregnant, nonlactating, average-risk adult women age 30 to 39 with a new persistent palpable breast mass and no overt inflammatory findings.

claims.statement: A deep partial-thickness burn involving the hand warrants burn-center consultation for transfer planning.
claims.limitation: Consultation and transfer are distinct decisions shaped by the receiving center and local resources. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with deep partial-thickness hand burns.

claims.statement: Deep partial-thickness burns tend to be paler or drier, less blanching, and less sensate; full-thickness burns are dry or leathery, nonblanching, and insensate.
claims.limitation: Burn depth can be mixed or evolve. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with thermal burns.

claims.statement: Burn-center consultation or transfer depends on depth, extent, special location, mechanism, inhalation concern, comorbidity, pain, local resources, and associated trauma; consultation does not make every small burn an automatic transfer.
claims.limitation: No unsourced numeric threshold or general treatment algorithm is taught. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with burns evaluated in a general clinic or emergency handoff.

claims.statement: A superficial partial-thickness burn is typically moist, red, blanching, blistered, and very painful; depth can evolve and requires reassessment.
claims.limitation: Individual findings are interpreted together rather than as absolute rules. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with thermal burns.

claims.statement: In a usual adult pathway, positive compatible serology leads to upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies for diagnostic confirmation.
claims.limitation: This does not assert that every adult in every setting must undergo biopsy. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with positive celiac serology and adequate total IgA in a routine diagnostic pathway.

claims.statement: Starting gluten avoidance before diagnostic testing can alter serologic and biopsy results.
claims.limitation: The content does not prescribe a gluten challenge. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: People undergoing evaluation for possible celiac disease.

claims.statement: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 typing addresses genetic susceptibility and does not by itself establish active celiac disease.
claims.limitation: This claim does not specify test performance or every clinical use of HLA typing. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: People undergoing evaluation for possible celiac disease.

claims.statement: IgG-based celiac serology has a limited diagnostic role when IgA deficiency makes IgA-based tests unreliable.
claims.limitation: This does not make an IgG panel the preferred routine first test before total IgA context is known. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: People evaluated for celiac disease when IgA deficiency is present or suspected.

claims.statement: While a patient is eating gluten, tTG-IgA together with total-IgA context is a usual initial serologic assessment for suspected celiac disease.
claims.limitation: IgA deficiency changes test selection; serology is not presented as universally definitive. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible symptoms who remain on gluten during diagnostic evaluation.

claims.statement: Suspected postoperative chylous ascites requires diagnostic fluid sampling with triglyceride measurement and studies directed at infection and other plausible postoperative leaks rather than diagnosis from imaging appearance alone.
claims.limitation: The exact ancillary fluid studies depend on the operation and differential diagnosis. This approved concept does not teach an unsourced universal numeric triglyceride cutoff. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults with newly identified ascites and suspected lymphatic leakage.

claims.statement: Cross-sectional imaging can demonstrate and localize ascites but cannot by appearance alone establish that the fluid is chylous.
claims.limitation: Imaging remains useful for extent, associated pathology, and procedural planning; this claim addresses fluid composition rather than overall imaging utility. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with postoperative intraperitoneal fluid under evaluation for possible chylous ascites.

claims.statement: In the approved population, adding prophylactic splenectomy increases operative morbidity while spleen preservation maintains oncologic survival.
claims.limitation: The package does not teach exact complication rates or substitute this population-level result for individualized operative planning. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the approved proximal-gastric-cancer operative population.

claims.statement: Routine prophylactic splenectomy does not improve survival during curative gastrectomy for resectable proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.
claims.limitation: This claim applies to prophylactic splenectomy in the defined proximal-gastric-cancer population and must not be generalized to every gastric tumor or to a therapeutic splenectomy indication. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing curative resection for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

claims.statement: The spleen-preservation teaching point is not a rule that splenectomy is never appropriate; direct splenic invasion, greater-curvature invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease falls outside the approved routine-prophylaxis scenario.
claims.limitation: Falling outside this scope does not by itself prescribe splenectomy; the specific operative decision remains separately authored clinical content. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for curative proximal gastric-cancer surgery.

claims.statement: Gastroparesis is diagnosed in a patient with compatible upper gastrointestinal symptoms by documenting objectively delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: Compatible symptoms alone are not diagnostic, and this concept assumes that an appropriate prior evaluation has already excluded mechanical obstruction. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic nausea, vomiting, early satiety, or postprandial fullness and no demonstrated mechanical gastric-outlet obstruction.

claims.statement: Four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy is the preferred objective study in this concept for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claims.limitation: The 2022 ACG guideline recommends solid-meal scintigraphy for at least three hours, while the 2025 AGA guideline specifically favors four-hour testing over studies lasting two hours or less. This concept does not teach an exact abnormal-retention cutoff. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing objective evaluation for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.

claims.statement: Upper endoscopy can help exclude mechanical obstruction but does not replace objective gastric emptying measurement; esophageal manometry and ambulatory pH monitoring evaluate different physiologic questions.
claims.limitation: Other validated gastric-emptying modalities may have selected roles. They are not taught or used as false distractors in this narrowly approved scintigraphic-testing concept. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing outpatient evaluation for suspected gastroparesis.

claims.statement:
RAI is a nonsurgical, disease-directed treatment that destroys overactive
thyroid cells. Antithyroid drugs reduce thyroid-hormone production, while
beta-blocking medicines can control symptoms without reducing hormone
production.
claims.limitation:
distinguishes the broad roles of these options for the
  counseling question; it does not specify a dose, preparation regimen,
  treatment timeline, or universal treatment preference. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claims.statement:
Current breastfeeding contraindicates therapeutic iodine-131 treatment for a
patient with Graves disease.
claims.limitation:
applies to therapeutic iodine-131; it does not prohibit
  counseling, referral, or individualized endocrine and pediatric guidance. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claims.statement:
A low TSH result with a high free T4 result is a biochemical pattern of thyroid
hormone excess; those functional results do not by themselves identify Graves
disease as the cause.
claims.limitation:
qualitative functional context only; this draft does
  not teach thresholds, severity classification, or a treatment decision. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claims.statement: When reduced plasma bicarbonate suggests metabolic acidosis, blood-gas assessment confirms the acidemia and identifies respiratory or mixed acid-base contributions.
claims.limitation: R1.1 is expert opinion; arterial sampling is not claimed universally superior. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with reduced plasma bicarbonate and suspected metabolic acidosis.

claims.statement: Peritoneal CO2 absorption adds a CO2 load; when pulmonary elimination does not match that load, blood CO2 can rise and produce respiratory acidemia.
claims.limitation: Ventilation and respiratory mechanics also affect blood CO2. The current observational study cannot establish every mechanistic contribution; these cases supply completed-care records rather than asking the clinic to select ventilator settings or manage live hypercarbia. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a resolved CO2-associated event in an outside anesthesia record.

claims.statement: Mixing studies are incompletely standardized, cannot by themselves establish or exclude acquired hemophilia A, and should not replace appropriate parallel factor assays.
claims.limitation: No universal correction threshold or isolated-aPTT bleeding-risk estimate is inferred. Interpretation remains tied to the laboratory method and clinical context. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with an outside specialist workup of an unexplained prolonged aPTT.

claims.statement: An aPTT mixing study evaluates the aPTT response after combining patient plasma with normal plasma; immediate and incubated assessments can reveal different inhibitory patterns.
claims.limitation: Qualitative method only. No mixing ratio, incubation duration, temperature or correction threshold is specified. Neither platelet testing nor a patient-only repeat is that plasma comparison. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults reviewing the purpose or method of an outside specialist mixing assessment.

claims.statement: Initial correction followed by loss of correction after incubation can indicate a time-dependent inhibitor; immediate correction alone does not exclude that possibility.
claims.limitation: No exact incubation period, temperature, ratio or laboratory cutoff is authored. A qualitative pattern suggests a mechanism and requires appropriate factor/inhibitor assessment; it is not a definitive diagnosis. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing immediate versus incubated results from a specialist coagulation laboratory.

claims.statement: A cancer metastasis retains the identity of its established primary cancer; its new anatomic location does not by itself make it a primary cancer of that organ.
claims.limitation: Current NCI explanation directly supports primary identity and naming after metastatic spread. The cases give a specialist pathology comparison confirming the relationship to a known cutaneous primary. No unknown-primary ranking, diagnosis from one stain, melanoma subtype inference or management decision. Unchanged offline recorded statement; original check/access dates retained. Exact N1 round-two application and source currentness remain unverified.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a confirmed metastasis from a supplied known primary.

claims.statement: Core needle biopsy may be appropriate for selected neck masses when the tissue or ancillary testing needed is not adequately supplied by fine-needle aspiration.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; core is acknowledged in feedback and is never an incorrect alternative to FNA. The cases do not ask for lymphoma-specific sampling or prescribe open biopsy after a fixed number of attempts. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Specialist-assessed neck masses with technique selection based on pathology requirements.

claims.statement: Cross-sectional neck imaging characterizes anatomy, whereas cell or tissue sampling supplies the material for a cytological or histological diagnosis of an undiagnosed suspicious neck mass.
claims.limitation: Single guideline's independently synthesized distinction between imaging and needle-sampling roles. A supplied CT description does not substitute for a tissue specimen; no universal sequence or guaranteed sampling result is claimed. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with an imaged but still undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass.

claims.statement: After appropriate assessment of an undiagnosed at-risk adult neck mass, fine-needle aspiration is an appropriate initial needle-sampling approach; open incisional or excisional biopsy should not replace the initial needle approach.
claims.limitation: Single independent guideline. FNA is the best offered needle option, not universally preferable to core biopsy. The game action is specialist referral, not a fabricated local generic-FNA procedure or a complete cancer-workup sequence. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with an assessed, undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass requiring an initial needle sample.

claims.statement: Reduced hemoglobin can reduce blood oxygen-carrying content even when the remaining hemoglobin has a normal oxygen saturation, so a normal SpO2 alone does not exclude anemia or establish adequate oxygen content.
claims.limitation: Qualitative physiological inference from independently verified hemoglobin-carriage and saturation-fraction facts; FDA device background also describes reduced oxygen-carrying ability in anemia. Other determinants of tissue oxygen delivery are not assessed. No numeric content equation, hemoglobin threshold or treatment decision. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with established anemia discussing an outside blood-count result.

claims.statement: An ordinary pulse-oximeter display can report oxygen saturation and pulse rate, sometimes with signal strength; those displayed values do not provide a hemoglobin concentration.
claims.limitation: FDA 2025 consumer page is the sole direct source for ordinary clip display fields. Cases explicitly supply those fields only. This does not claim that every specialized multi-parameter device lacks additional functions, and it does not order a new blood test. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting supplied ordinary pulse-oximeter display values.

claims.statement: Hemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen, and its blood concentration is a separate quantity from the percentage oxygen saturation.
claims.limitation: NHLBI December 2025 CBC explanation verifies hemoglobin carriage; FDA background verifies saturation's proportional meaning. Original qualitative comparison, without a numeric anemia threshold, race-specific reference range, transfusion indication or claim about cardiac output. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied outside hemoglobin result and saturation reading.

claims.statement: Pulse-oximeter SpO2 estimates the proportion of hemoglobin oxygen-binding capacity occupied by oxygen, expressed as a percentage.
claims.limitation: FDA 2024 executive-summary Introduction supplies the hemoglobin-fraction explanation; FDA 2025 consumer page independently confirms the percentage estimate. SpO2 is an estimate with device limitations, not a direct measurement of blood oxygen content or tissue delivery. No formula or fixed normal threshold. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting an ordinary supplied pulse-oximeter reading.

claims.statement: Simple cholecystectomy may suffice after complete removal of margin-negative incidental T1a gallbladder carcinoma.
claims.limitation: Older specialist guideline cross-checked against 2025 society guidance. This applies only to confirmed completely resected T1a disease; uncertain depth, positive margins, residual disease and T1b or deeper disease need a different specialist plan. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claims.statement: Uncertain depth, positive margins or residual gallbladder carcinoma require a different specialist assessment.
claims.limitation: Older specialist guideline cross-checked against 2025 society guidance. This applies only to confirmed completely resected T1a disease; uncertain depth, positive margins, residual disease and T1b or deeper disease need a different specialist plan. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claims.statement: Gallbladder carcinoma invading the muscular layer is T1b.
claims.limitation: Only the local pathologic T category is assigned; node status, metastasis and full stage grouping are not inferred from wall depth alone. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claims.statement: Meeting standard Milan criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but does not by itself guarantee listing or transplantation; disease outside Milan criteria may still warrant specialist evaluation of other pathways.
claims.limitation: This concept intentionally excludes AFP policy, downstaging selection, organ allocation, liver function, comorbid contraindications, and individualized treatment choice. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying standard Milan criteria without equating a tumor-burden classification with automatic listing or permanent exclusion.

claims.statement: Standard Milan classification requires no macrovascular invasion and no extrahepatic disease.
claims.limitation: Microscopic pathology, transplant-center assessment, tumor biology, and other candidacy factors are outside this narrow recognition concept. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma whose staging is being compared with standard Milan criteria.

claims.statement: Standard Milan tumor-burden criteria for hepatocellular carcinoma comprise one lesion measuring 1 through 5 cm, or two to three lesions each measuring 1 through 3 cm.
claims.limitation: This claim describes the standard tumor-number and size envelope; it is not a complete transplant-candidacy or organ-allocation rule. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
